children: Hindustan Unilever Ltd’s (HUL) new growth strategy has drawn mostly constructive analyst views on the company’s prospects, but with some caution over higher investments and a wider margin band. The FMCG major’s shares traded moderately lower on Monday, after the company’s Capital Markets Day announcements.

The HUL stock was down 0.55 percent at Rs 1,962.5 in morning trade. The decline came amid a softer broader market. At 9:34 am, the Nifty 50 was down 0.28 percent at 23,831, while the Sensex declined 199 points to 76,316. The stock has fallen around 15 percent so far in 2026, substantially underperforming the Nifty 50, which is down 8.6 percent over the same period. The FMCG major’s market capitalisation stands at just under Rs 4.64 lakh crore.

Brokerages were largely positive following HUL’s Capital Markets Day, with Jefferies, Nomura and HSBC retaining their ‘buy’ calls. Their target prices of Rs 2,440-2,450 imply roughly 24-25 percent upside from Friday’s closing price. Morgan Stanley remained ‘equal-weight’ with a target of Rs 2,480, while CLSA was the most cautious, retaining a ‘hold’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,804.
HUL stock call: Jefferies sees sharper, segment-led growth strategy

Jefferies retained its ‘buy’ rating on HUL but cut its target price to Rs 2,450. The brokerage said the company’s ‘New India’ strategy marks a shift away from a broad-based approach towards sharper, segment-led growth.

title: HUL stock outlook: Brokerages see up to 26% upside as FMCG major sharpens ‘New India’ growth strategy
